channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Saudi Arabia closes East-West pipeline as Houthis tighten grip on Red Sea
item.description: Saudi Arabia on Saturday ​shut down the vital East-West pipeline after the conduit came under attack in the widening Middle East war, threatening to send energy prices soaring. The 1,200-km pipeline has served as the main route out for global ​supplies of Middle East oil for the ‌past six months while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by war.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Céline Dion makes historic Paris comeback, six years after last tour
item.description: Beloved French Canadian singer Céline Dion on Saturday returned to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder with a sell-out concert in an arena west of Paris. The 58-year-old appeared visibly moved as she opened her first full concert in six years to a crowd of around 30,000 people.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Danish WWII drama wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
item.description: A Danish WWII drama about a woman trying to hide a wartime relationship with a Nazi was awared top prize on Saturday at The Venice Film Festival, while Gaza documentary NAZA snagged the special jury prize. "Unknown Woman" had been a major talking point of the festival due to its subject matter, which has rarely been explored in film, and because director May el-Toukhy was almost alone as a woman director in the event.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Tens of thousands protest against far-right AfD party in Germany
item.description: About 150,000 demonstrators took to the streets in around 20 cities across Germany on Saturday against the far-right AfD, after the party scored a crushing victory in a state election last week. The Alternative for Germany (AfD) topped the vote in the eastern region of Saxony-Anhalt, and is now seeking to form the first extreme-right state government in Germany since World War II.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: France beats Germany to reach first women's World Cup basketball final
item.description: France beat Germany Saturday and made it through to the final of the women's basketball World Cup for the first time after a 86-64 victory. Gabby Williams top scored with 22 points for the Olympic silver medalists, who kept their unbeaten record at the tournament alive before Sunday's decider in Berlin.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Kenya: Crocodiles pushed towards homes by rising lakes
item.description: Climate change is forcing Kenya's wildlife officers to go on a crocodile hunt on the shores of Lake Baringo in a bid to curb growing human-wildlife conflict. Lakes in Kenya's Rift Valley have risen to levels not seen in at least half a century, pushing the reptiles towards human homes. Officers are tasked with trapping the animals and relocating them — an operation as tricky as it is dangerous.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump in Ireland: What are Irish people saying about the visit?
item.description: US President Donald Trump held talks Saturday in Dublin with his Irish counterpart Catherine Connolly during a weekend visit that's more about a major golf tournament hosted on a course he owns on the country's Atlantic coast. He also met with Ireland's Prime Minister Micheál Martin. We discuss that with Gavin Cooney, sports correspondent at the Irish Times.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'The excitement is just too much!': Céline Dion poised for emotional comeback in Paris
item.description: Celine Dion was set to make her long-awaited return to the stage in Paris on Saturday after years of battling a rare neurological disorder, with anticipation among fans reaching fever pitch. "The excitement is just too much!" a fan told our journalist Jennifer Ben Brahim.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French police suspect train derailment was sabotage
item.description: French investigators suspect sabotage was behind a train derailment in northwestern France that injured 44 people and left passengers in a state of shock, prosecutors said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: BRICS: What is in the joint statement from the 11 members?
item.description:
Members of the 11-nation BRICS group including China, Russia, Iran and India called for calm in the Middle East at a summit in New Delhi on Saturday, overcoming earlier divisions to issue a joint statement.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, who joined Russian, Iranian, Indian and other leaders in India's capital, told the summit that the Middle East war "does not serve the common interests of the international community".
France 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Anthropic boss calls for AI slowdown, Altman and Musk agree
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on artificial intelligence (AI) firms to slow down the development of the powerful technology, amid mounting worries over the risks of "superintelligent" computer systems.

item.title: Céline Dion's comeback: Why did she choose Paris?
item.description: Céline Dion was set to make her long-awaited return to the stage in Paris on Saturday after years of battling a rare neurological disorder, with fans counting down the hours until showtime. But why did she choose this city? "It's not just the Olympics effect. Paris was the launch pad for her career. Beyond Quebec, through the '80s and early '90s, commentators have always mentioned that Paris is like a second home for her," says our guest Nick Rees-Roberts, professor of media, culture and communication at Sorbonne Nouvelle University.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: AfD leads in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Merz's CDU slumps to 7%
item.description: Germany's far-right AfD is leading in polls ahead of regional elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania on September 20, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz's centre-right CDU has fallen to just 7%, according to a new ZDF poll. The result would mark the party's worst-ever showing in a regional election in Germany.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Africa: Rethinking the city of tomorrow
item.description: How should we envision the African city of tomorrow? A city adapted to population growth and climate change, and freed from a colonial past that is still very much present in some places. Africa’s first pan-African architecture biennale, held this week in Kenya, is seeking to answer that question.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Senegal: Building a home-grown space industry
item.description:
Africa’s space ambitions are gathering pace, and Senegal is determined not just to put satellites into orbit, but to build them at home.
Senegalese engineers are already mastering satellite manufacturing in France, with the goal of bringing that expertise back to their country and developing a home-grown space industry.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Niger: Kafra oil block could hold 2.5 billion barrels
item.description: Niger’s oil minister held a press conference on Wednesday to address a key issue for the country: the oil reserves Niger could rely on to fuel its development. Most of Niger’s oil production is currently operated by Chinese companies, but one area — the Kafra oil block — could become a cornerstone of economic cooperation with neighbouring Algeria. Active drilling has begun in the block, with the minister announcing that the zone could hold an estimated 2.5 billion barrels of oil. Our correspondent Harold Girard tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: DR Congo: At least 24 children die in school fire
item.description: At least 24 children have died after a fire broke out at a school in Bukavu, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The blaze reportedly started while children were in class, with some attempting to escape by jumping from higher floors. Adults are also reported to have died, while an investigation into the cause of the fire is underway. Our correspondent Emmet Livingstone tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump begins two-day Ireland visit, security operation costs €20 million
item.description: US President Donald Trump arrives in Dublin for a two-day visit to Ireland, where he is expected to meet Irish leaders and spend time at his golf resort in Doonbeg, County Clare. His visit has prompted a major security operation reportedly costing €20 million, while opinions remain divided among locals.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
item.description: Leaders of the BRICS nations are meeting in New Delhi on Saturday for a summit focused on trade, investment and global conflicts, as the bloc seeks a bigger role in shaping the global agenda for emerging and developing countries. Our correspondent Navodita Kumari tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Houthis seize key sites around Bab el-Mandeb as Saudi oil exports face disruption
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has stopped transferring oil through a major pipeline after it was attacked by drones.
Meanwhile, Houthi forces have taken control of a strategic port and island in Bab el-Mandeb from Yemeni government forces.
Iran, which backs the rebels, says it had nothing to do with the attacks.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Russia's Putin arrives in India as BRICS leaders begin talks
item.description: President Putin arrived as talks among leaders of the BRICS diplomatic bloc began on Friday in India, amid global geopolitical turmoil, including the war in Ukraine and the conflict in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
